column1: # RacingSim binary asset ownership claims
# Enforced by .githooks/pre-commit. Activate the hook with:
#     git config core.hooksPath .githooks
# Why this file exists: hard constraint #7 forbids parallel edits to .uasset/.umap,
# and BLOCKER-002 means git-lfs locking cannot enforce it (no LFS-capable remote, so
# `git lfs lock` fails with "missing protocol"). This is the interim enforcement:
# claim before you edit, and the hook blocks any staged binary asset that is unclaimed
# or claimed by someone else.
# It is NOT a substitute for locking. It cannot coordinate across machines or clones.
# It is a real gate on this clone, which is where the project works today. When D-2 is
# decided -- LFS remote, Perforce, or formal acceptance of process-only serialization --
# revisit whether this file stays.
# Format, TAB-separated. First matching glob wins.
#     <path-glob>
# <path-glob> is matched with shell case-globbing against the repo-relative path, so
# Content/Cars/* matches one level and Content/Cars/*/* matches deeper. Use the
# broadest glob that covers the ticket's scope, not one line per file.
# <owner> must equal the committer's `git config user.name` exactly.
# Example, once content exists:
#     Content/Cars/Prototype/*
#     Content/Tracks/Prototype/*
# Claims
# TRACK-002, 2026-08-19. The first binary asset in the repository:
# Content/Tracks/Prototype/Maps/L_Meridian_Graybox.umap, the graybox test level.
# The graybox level was TRACK-001's acceptance criterion and was deferred into
# TRACK-002's scope by director ruling (Docs/Tickets.md), so that the ticket which
# places checkpoint gates also owns the map's authoring, serialisation and license
# posture as one unit.
# Before claiming, the whole worktree tree was searched for .uasset/.umap:
#     find .claude/worktrees -path "*/Content/*" -type f
# returned only Content/Tests/.gitkeep and Content/Tests/README.md across all 17
# worktrees. No other agent held Unreal content at the time of this claim.
# The glob is Content/Tracks/Prototype/* rather than the single map file: the same
# directory will take the sector/road/graybox-art assets a later track ticket adds,
# and one claim per file is how a claim table stops being read.
Content/Tracks/Prototype/*
Content/Tracks/Prototype/*/*
